title: "Mathematical Foundations for AI"
subtitle: "IIT Gandhinagar · Prof. Nipun Batra"
---

::: {.hero-section}

A 26-lecture, 80-minutes-each course that builds the mathematical stack of modern AI — floating point, linear algebra, multivariate calculus and automatic differentiation, probability and estimation, optimization, information theory, and Markov chains.

Every concept arrives **picture → numbers → code → symbols**. The destination: by the last lecture you train a character-level language model from scratch — a Markov chain, fit by maximum likelihood, scored by cross-entropy, optimized by gradient descent, differentiated automatically, computed in floating point. Every module is a prerequisite for that one artifact.

:::

## How to use this site
Each lecture row links its slides (PDF, one page per slide), companion notebook, and interactive. Tutorials are hybrid: a pen-and-paper worksheet plus a Jupyter notebook, both published. All four textbooks are **free PDFs** — see [Resources](resources.qmd).
:::

---

## Textbook backbone

The course follows **Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong · *Mathematics for Machine Learning*** (free PDF). Optimization leans on Boyd & Vandenberghe, information theory on MacKay, numerics on Solomon.

| Role | Resource |
|------|----------|
| **Primary** — assigned reading | [Deisenroth et al., *Mathematics for Machine Learning*](https://mml-book.github.io/) — free PDF |
| **Optimization** | [Boyd & Vandenberghe, *Convex Optimization*](https://stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/) — free PDF |
| **Information theory** | [MacKay, *Information Theory, Inference and Learning Algorithms*](https://www.inference.org.uk/itprnn/book.pdf) — free PDF + [video lectures](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLruBu5BI5n4aFpG32iMbdWoRVAA-Vcso6) |
| **Numerics** | [Solomon, *Numerical Algorithms*](https://people.csail.mit.edu/jsolomon/share/book/numerical_book.pdf) — free PDF |
| **Visual intuition** | 3Blue1Brown, [Essence of Linear Algebra](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/linear-algebra) · [Essence of Calculus](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/calculus) |

## The destination thread

One artifact grows across the semester — the character-level language model:

**L2** log-space numerics → **L5/L25** transition matrices & stationary eigenvectors → **L11** gradients through the loss → **L14** fitting = MLE → **L17** gradient descent finds the parameters → **L24** cross-entropy & perplexity → **L26** trained, sampled, understood.
